insights.title: Regulated digital-assets shipping is a scarce genome
insights.text: Very few product leaders have shipped a 10-product, $7B regulated crypto suite inside SEC/FINRA controls. That is the exact terrain Kinexys operates in. The differentiator is not 'crypto-curious' — it is 'has already shipped compliant digital-assets product at institutional scale.'

insights.title: JPM is buying de-risking, not vision
insights.text: At a bank, a VP PM in a digital-assets group is hired to ship inside heavy governance without breaking anything — cost, risk, reliability metrics are named in the JD before customer value. Lead with 'policy-at-the-glass / compliance-in-the-loop' proof, not 0-to-1 founder energy.

next_steps.text: If a screen lands: reframe the resume's lead from MCP/agents to the Grayscale regulated digital-assets record (P3). The resume-amex-mcp tailor is WRONG for this one — needs a resume-kinexys / regulated-digital-assets cut.
Pre-empt the matrix-org objection (P2): have one crisp story of shipping through a big-org compliance/legal/risk gauntlet on schedule (Grayscale release train, 4 time zones, -35% cycle time).
Warm-path check: query LinkedIn network for JPM/Kinexys connections before the recruiter call (application already in — a referral still helps surface it).

blocks.intro: Kinexys = JPM's blockchain / digital-assets division (formerly Onyx): DLT, tokenization, Web3 banking rails, payments.

items.html: Domain 1:1 with Grayscale — regulated digital-assets product at institutional scale is the exact genome; very few PMs have actually shipped it.
JD orders cost/risk/reliability BEFORE customer value — this is a de-risking hire; governance is the product.
Preferred: matrixed-org experience — the tell that internal navigation, not raw building, is the day-job.
VP at a bank ≈ senior IC/lead — appropriate level for a 20-yr operator; not a demotion despite 'mid-senior' label.

blocks.intro: Steer toward domain proof; pre-empt the matrix objection.

items.html: Ask: how much of this role is net-new product vs. hardening existing rails? · look for: real 0→1 surface, not pure backlog-tending.
Ask: where does the compliance/legal/risk gate sit in the SDLC? · look for: a mature 'compliance-in-the-loop' cadence I can plug into.
Landmine: leading with the ARCS MCP/agent story — wrong surface here; it reads as off-domain enthusiasm. Lead Grayscale.
Landmine: founder/high-autonomy framing that signals 'won't thrive in a matrix.' Show I ship THROUGH governance, not around it.

items.html: BAR (ruin): low ruin — application already submitted, sunk cost is near-zero. The only real cost is over-investing prep on a role that may be an internal fill. Cap prep until a human responds.

LAB · Loki: 'You're a founder who'll suffocate in a bank's matrix and leave in 18 months.' Steel-manned down: true risk, but Grayscale (DCG-owned, regulated) proves I ship inside institutional governance — name it before they raise it.

COURT: honesty check — the Grayscale claims are documented/self-reported and true; do NOT stretch 'crypto fundamentals' into implying protocol-engineering depth I don't have. Product + regulated shipping is the honest lane.

p: If the 3-week falsifier fires (no response), that is high-information, not failure: it says domain fit alone doesn't clear JPM's filter and the resume lead (or an internal-fill reality) is the real variable — which sharpens every future bank application.
